label: kkonai
title: っこない
meaning_example: I cant possibly get a Nobel prize

notes.text:
＊If you wish to use this more politely, 「っこありません」is acceptable.



FORMATION:

Ｖ(minus ます) + っこない



＊「できっこない」、「わかりっこない」、or other verbs of possibility are often used.
notes.html:
＊If you wish to use this more politely, 「っこありません」is acceptable.

FORMATION:

＊「できっこない」、「わかりっこない」、or other verbs of possibility are often used.

comments.text:
note : potential = 可能法

可能動詞：ex「読む」「書く」に対する「読める」「書ける」などの類。命令形をもたない。
comments.html:
note : potential = 可能法
可能動詞：ex「読む」「書く」に対する「読める」「書ける」などの類。命令形をもたない。

comments.text: → Potential form : Ex. kaku (write) → kakeru (able to write), yomu (read) → yomeru (able to read) and such forms.  There is no imperative form for potential verbs.  [e.g. You cant say "You! Be able to read!" ;-) ]

comments.text: ろ I think is a particle which attach to the imperative form of verb to show it is an order. It used to be a dialect of Kanto area in the old days, but became popular even in Kyoto during the Middle Ages (12th Century to 16th Century in Japan).
comments.html: ろ I think is a particle which attach to the imperative form of verb to show it is an order. It used to be a dialect of Kanto area in the old days, but became popular even in Kyoto during the Middle Ages (12th Century to 16th Century in Japan).

comments.text: That means 読め(+ろ)、書け(+ろ) are imperative form of 読む、書く and are not of potential verbs 読める、書ける. With this, you can exaplin 歌え+ろよand 歌えれ+よ(imperative form for potentioal verb, too. The former of dictional form is 歌う and the latter is 歌える（可能動詞）. どうでしょうか？
